title: A peaceful panorama on Maunakea
caption: The Milky Way and the zodiacal light over Gemini North and UKIRT, Maunakea, Hawai‘i
credit: International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava)

recognition.text: NOIRLab Image of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The glowing arch of the Milky Way spans this wide panorama from Maunakea in Hawai‘i, with Gemini North at the far right and the United Kingdom Infrared Telescope on the left. In the middle, the last pastel light of sunset fades on the horizon.

Rising from the horizon and seeming to cut through the Milky Way is the zodiacal light, a faint glow of sunlight scattered off dust between the planets. The Milky Way is really a flat disk, and across a small patch of sky it looks straight; it only bends into an arch here because the picture covers so much of the sky at once.

Gemini North is one half of the International Gemini Observatory, operated by NOIRLab. The photograph was taken during NOIRLab’s 2022 expedition to all of its observing sites, by Petr Horálek, one of its Audiovisual Ambassadors.

understand.summary: A ground-based landscape photograph credited to International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA/P. Horálek (Institute of Physics in Opava). The source does not publish camera, exposure or color-processing details.
understand.eye: A camera can gather light for longer than the eye, so the Milky Way looks brighter and more detailed here than it would to someone standing on site.

explore: The zodiacal light is easiest to see from very dark sites after evening twilight or before dawn, rising along the path the Sun and planets follow across the sky.
alt: A wide panorama of a mountaintop at night, with telescope domes at both ends, the Milky Way arching across the sky and a faint cone of light rising from the horizon.
